summary: Documents version 2 of the Internet Group Management Protocol, which hosts use to tell nearby routers which multicast groups they belong to. It updates RFC 1112. Version 2 adds improvements such as leaving a group more quickly.

plainLanguage.summary: IGMPv2 lets a computer tell its nearby router which multicast groups it wants to receive. When the last known listener leaves, the router can check quickly and stop forwarding that group's traffic to the local network.

questions: how do hosts join multicast groups
how do hosts join a multicast group
what is the igmp leave group message
how does igmpv2 report a group leave
subtitle: How hosts announce multicast group membership to nearby routers and how routers check whether anyone remains.

tldr.problem: Multicast routers need to know which groups have listeners on each attached network. IGMPv1 did not let a host report that it was the last member leaving, so routers could keep forwarding traffic until a membership timer expired.
tldr.mechanism: IGMPv2 routers send queries and hosts answer after random delays. A Leave Group message lets the querier send group-specific queries and check whether members remain.
tldr.outcome: RFC 2236 updates RFC 1112 and adds faster leave reporting and a querier-election procedure. It has since been updated by RFC 3376 and RFC 9776.

today: RFC 2236 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 1112. It has been updated by RFC 3376 and RFC 9776.

sections.title: What IGMP Reports
sections.content:
The Internet Group Management Protocol (IGMP) lets IP hosts report multicast group membership to immediately neighboring multicast routers. This RFC defines the host-to-router exchange; it does not specify how routers use IGMP with one another.

IGMP is carried in IP with protocol number 2. The messages in this specification use an IP time-to-live of 1 and include the IP Router Alert option. IGMPv2 updates RFC 1112 and adds a way to report group departure quickly.
sections.plainLanguage: IGMP is how a computer tells a nearby router that it wants a multicast group. The router uses these reports to decide which groups have listeners on the local network.

sections.title: The Eight-Octet Message
sections.content:
An IGMP message has a Type, Max Response Time, Checksum and Group Address field. The host-router messages are Membership Query (0x11), Version 2 Membership Report (0x16) and Leave Group (0x17); Version 1 Membership Report (0x12) remains for compatibility.

A General Query uses a zero group address to ask about all memberships on the network. A Group-Specific Query names one group. Max Response Time applies to queries and is measured in tenths of a second. The checksum covers the entire IGMP message.
sections.plainLanguage: Each message names its purpose and the group it concerns. A query asks hosts to report, a report announces membership, and a leave message says a host is departing.

sections.title: Queries, Reports and Leaving
sections.content:
For each attached network, routers elect a querier: a router hearing a query from a lower IP address becomes a non-querier. The querier periodically sends a General Query to 224.0.0.1. A host starts a separate random response timer for each group it belongs to.

When a timer expires, the host reports membership to that group. If it hears another host's report first, it cancels its own timer, suppressing duplicate reports. On leaving, the last host known to have reported should send a Leave Group message to 224.0.0.2; the querier then sends group-specific queries to check for remaining members.
sections.plainLanguage: The querier asks which groups have listeners, and hosts spread their replies over a random delay. If one host answers for a group, the others can stay quiet; a leave makes the router check again.

sections.title: Working with IGMPv1 Devices
sections.content:
A host on a network with an IGMPv1 querier must interpret a query whose Max Response Time is zero as 100, or 10 seconds, and send Version 1 reports while that router is considered present. The host may skip Leave messages in this mode.

An IGMPv2 router sharing a network with an IGMPv1 router must be configured to use IGMPv1, because the RFC says there is no reliable way to detect such routers dynamically. A router that hears a Version 1 report must track that older membership and ignore Leave messages for that group while the compatibility timer runs.
sections.plainLanguage: Older routers and hosts do not understand every IGMPv2 message. When an older version is present, devices use the older report behavior and avoid relying on the faster leave procedure.

sections.title: Timers and Message Destinations
sections.content:
Most IGMP timers can be configured, but non-default values must be consistent among routers on one link. The default Robustness Variable is 2, and the default Query Interval is 125 seconds. The Query Response Interval defaults to 100 units, which is 10 seconds.

The Last Member Query Interval defaults to 10 units, or 1 second, and affects how quickly a querier can confirm that a group has no members. General Queries go to 224.0.0.1; leave messages go to the all-routers group at 224.0.0.2.
sections.plainLanguage: Timers control how often routers ask and how long they wait for replies. Shorter last-member checks can reduce the time before the router learns that nobody remains in a group.

sections.title: Forged Queries and Reports
sections.content:
A forged query from a lower IP address can make an attacker the querier. Forged reports can make a router believe that a group has listeners, while a forged Version 1 report can cause it to ignore leave messages. A forged leave causes extra queries but does not by itself remove desired traffic.

The RFC suggests checking that report and leave source addresses belong to the subnet of the receiving interface, or ignoring messages without the Router Alert option. Ignoring Version 1 reports can also reduce one risk, but it breaks automatic compatibility with Version 1 hosts.
sections.plainLanguage: A false query or report can change what the router believes about group membership. Checking message sources can reduce this risk, though some checks affect compatibility with older hosts.

fields.name: Type
fields.desc: Query, membership report or leave message.

fields.name: Checksum
fields.desc: Checksum over the complete IGMP message.

fields.name: Group Address
fields.desc: Zero for a General Query; otherwise the group address.
